PROVENANCE, STATED PLAINLY: the named specialists bubbles.simplify, bubbles.stabilize, bubbles.security and bubbles.audit DID NOT RUN. The work was performed by a general delivery agent dispatched under bubbles.goal, so this is a general-runner execution, NOT a specialist dispatch, and the agent field names the actual executor rather than a specialist that never ran. Consequence stated rather than engineered around: Gate G022 Check 6B resolves the owner of each of these four phases from workflows.yaml as a literal specialist (bubbles.simplify / bubbles.stabilize / bubbles.security / bubbles.audit), not as activeWorkflowRunner, so this truthful entry does NOT satisfy it and the gate still blocks. That is the correct outcome; renaming the agent to a specialist that did not run would defeat the gate with a false record, which is the same vacuous-signal failure this packet is about. Related observation, flagged not silently rewritten: the four report.md section headings still read 'bubbles.simplify', 'bubbles.stabilize', 'bubbles.security', 'bubbles.audit' and overstate attribution in the same way. (1) SIMPLIFY -- Finding S-1, FIXED: scripts/runtime/go-integration.sh closed with two consecutive if blocks testing the identical condition, 'if [[ "$go_test_rc" -ne 0 ]]', the first echoing and the second exiting. Nothing between the two blocks can change go_test_rc, so the split was pure duplication; merged into one block with identical behaviour, and the guard suite plus the full untagged suite were re-run at exit 0. (2) STABILIZE -- no flake source found. The gate marker check is a pure string assertion over an already-captured file, with no timing dependency; a scan of the added package found no socket, no sql/pgx, no docker and no exec.Command, so a deterministic classifier over a committed YAML file cannot flake and making the lane depend on it leaves it stricter, not less reliable. (3) SECURITY -- S-1: the gate marker echoes seven distinct variables (a fixed literal prefix, three integers, two exit codes, the operator's own -run regex, and the marker line, which by construction carries only counts and two floats) and NONE is secret-bearing; zero ':-' or '-' fallback expansions exist in the changed wrapper, so it cannot print a real value. S-2: the capture file is an mktemp path at mode 600, owner-only, outside the repo tree, and removed by cleanup_gate_output on EXIT -- with the honest caveat, recorded not glossed, that trap does not fire on SIGKILL, so a hard kill could strand one mode-600 file in /tmp. The file carries ZERO //go:build directives, so it genuinely is untagged and genuinely does sit in the unit lane, which is exactly what R6.4 requires. R6.4 is SATISFIED; the check was wrong. A guard keyed on a substring that also appears in prose is the same vacuous-signal failure this bug is about, so the false positive is reported rather than quietly dropped (report.md, Audit Record A-3). Verdict: FOUR of the five are genuinely new with no existing counterpart, and they compose rather than repeat -- evalLaneIsGateDiagnostic is built on evalLaneStderrDiagnostic, and evalLaneFirstGateDiagnostic reuses evalLaneIsGateDiagnostic. assertEvalLaneDualFailureReporting is a sibling of assertEvalLaneContract, not a duplicate: different arity, different invariant (ordering/masking vs presence), and merging them would force the A0 minimal fixture to satisfy an ordering contract it was not built for. The ONE real near-duplicate is requireEvalDualReportingBaselinePasses against requireEvalBaselinePasses: same four-line anti-tautology shape, differing only in which assert function is called and the message wording. NOT collapsed, with reasons: the two cannot drift into disagreement because each guards its own assert function, so unlike the S-2 marker case there is no correctness payoff; a collapsed form would have to take a pre-evaluated error, moving the assertion to the call site and making the precondition less self-documenting; and the new helper's own doc comment already says 'mirroring requireEvalBaselinePasses', so the parallelism is documented and deliberate rather than copy-paste. Decisive positive evidence that the addition was not duplicative: the new tests REUSE the pre-existing mutateEvalFixture and evalLaneSources instead of forking them. (6) NEW OBSERVATION, RECORDED NOT ACTED ON: the marker literal still has four sites, and two are Go constants in different packages -- evalGateMarkerPrefix in package deploy and GateMarkerPrefix in package assistanteval. tests/eval/assistant/harness.go is UNTAGGED, so an import is technically possible and would bind them. Deliberately NOT done: the guard today imports stdlib only (fmt, path/filepath, strings, testing) and its own header states it sits outside both halves on purpose, so importing assistanteval would make the guard's ability to compile and run depend on the gate package compiling -- an edit that broke the gate could then also disable the guard that exists to detect a disabled gate, which is the same failure shape this bug records. Honest counterweight, not suppressed: a precedent for internal/** importing the tests tree does exist (internal/agent/bug064003_router_warmup_contract_test.go), so the objection is guard independence, not layering novelty. The drift is already caught loudly at runtime -- rename the harness constant alone and the shell greps a prefix that is never emitted, producing 'the assistant acceptance gate did not run'. Later than guard time, but loud and correctly attributed, so this is an observation for design, not a defect. (7) INSPECTED AND DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED, each with a reason: the triple 'ERROR: --run requires a non-empty regex' is OUT OF BLAST RADIUS, proven by count 3 at c7667d99~1 and 3 now, with c7667d99's first hunk on that file opening at line 50, after the parsing block; the four repeated 'Unit evidence: internal/assistant/metrics/metrics_test.go' echoes in tests/e2e/assistant_regression_e2e_test.sh are likewise pre-existing at count 4 before and after; gate_marker_check_failed=1 appears four times but is NOT collapsible, since each of the four branches reports a distinct failure cause and the R3.5 invariant that this same file asserts (subtest A10) requires every flag-raise to be preceded by its own diagnostic, so collapsing them would break the contract the file exists to enforce; the two line-scanning loops inside assertEvalLaneDualFailureReporting share their offset bookkeeping but enforce independent invariants with different early-return semantics, and merging them would change which error surfaces first for the A8 and A10 mutations, which both operate on the same diagnostic line; and harness_test.go's inline corpora were left inline -- this CORRECTS the earlier pass's count of 'two', there are five inline corpora plus one Rows: nil construction, and each fixture's row count and label composition is itself the thing under test (four rows, two capture-expected, six assertions), so a shared builder would either break those arithmetic assertions or carry the same information at the call site. './smackerel.sh test unit --go --go-run TestEvalLaneContract' exits 0, with internal/deploy the only package NOT reporting '[no tests to run]', confirming the selector actually bound tests there. rootCause: Two mechanisms with complementary intent and no link between them. tests/eval/assistant/acceptance_test.go opted OUT of the untagged unit lane via //go:build integration on the stated assumption that the tagged integration lane would pick it up. scripts/runtime/go-integration.sh selects packages by an explicit allow-list, not ./..., and was never extended to include ./tests/eval/... A build tag can only include a file inside a package that was already selected, so the opt-out executed and the opt-in did not. Nothing asserts the pairing, so the assumption printed in the file's own header went stale with no surface turning red. The failure mode of a missing test is silence.
scopeOfClaim: This gate measures assistant routing accuracy and capture-fallback coverage on an offline corpus using the harness's deterministic keyword classifier as a structural proxy for the production router. It does NOT measure corpus-grant enforcement. The D25/D28 grant holes carried by spec 108 are a separate axis and are NOT made measurable by fixing this bug.
